Service is fantastic
Aug 2025 • Couples
We stayed at The Reverie for our trip to HCMC and the service was wonderful. The attached restaurant/bar here provided the same level of service. We sat outside on our first evening and enjoyed cocktails with steak. We have a favourite order (Champagne and Negroni, with still mineral water). We were well served by Yen and when we returned the next evening, she remembered our order. She was wonderful. The drinks were excellent and the food was also very good. We enjoyed a steak sharing platter - essentially steak for 3 shared between 2! The quality was very good and it was beautifully cooked - we like it rare and it was done to perfection. We also ate here on another evening and it was comparably good. It’s a great spot for sitting outside once the day cools and watching the world go by particularly when it’s a pedestrian evening. Highly recommend - not cheap but worth it for the service and the quality. Thank you to Yen!

I visited at the Long @ Time square several times during the lunch time, but also at dinner time. (great escape for rainy day)
Their food (drinks also) are very good value for the money. For example their midweek lunch 3 courses set menu deal 228000VND (9$) is very good. As it’s their Happy Hour deals (midweek 4pm-7pm) drinks are “buy one get one free” and weekend (11am-7pm) food and drinks are “buy one get one free”. And prices are very good, to consider that the long is part of the 6* hotel.
Their menu has wide range of something to everybody..local food, asian food, italia food, salads, small snacks etc. not forgetting their 16 different flavors gelato bar.
All my visits i was well take care of Ms. Ngoc and the other great staff that works there

I highly recommend to visit at the Long, if you are around city center of Ho Chi Minh.

Great for lunch, dinner, cafe, gelato, drinks, people-watching!
Dec 2023 • Friends
Fantastic lunch set. Something for everyone, with lots of options for both starter and main. The menu changes from time to time; some of my favorites have included chicken caprese, spaghetti putanesca, smoked salmon starters, crostini samplers... Theres a huge selection of gelato as an add-on if still hungry. I recommend the Tiramisu or Vietnamese Coffee flavors! Venue is covered so you're not sitting in the rain or getting a sun-burn, but both entrances are open, and the whole place has super-high ceilings, so it feels very well ventilated, like dining in an atrium. Fun fact - it goes from Nguyen Hue to Dong Khoi Sts - so the name fits! Highly recommended

Highly recommend. Yes it is pricey but the mocktail and food were good. Excellent service with a nice atmosphere.
Jan 2023 • Solo
I really liked this. I went twice. Yes it is pricey which many reviewers mention but look at the menu before going in. Not like they hide the price. They are part of a 5 star hotel THE REVERIE SAIGON so this is likely to be expensive. By Western standards not so much. They have a good drinks menu, plus food too. The atmosphere is lovely. Staff are really nice, pleasant and friendly. Good service. Clean. Nice location on the busy Walking Street but feels like another world away. There is loads of seating inside or outside. I always sat inside as it got windy a lot of evenings in Saigon. Go during Happy Hour which is 16:00 to 19:00 daily. Drinks are 50% off (excludes some drinks). The first time I went I had a quick drink before dinner somewhere else. The chia berries mix mocktail was one of the best I had. So good, well presented and refreshing. You get complimentary nuts and seeds or spicy something (couldn't make out what it was) with your drinks. The second time I went I had the same mocktail (it was so good) and a light appetizer of scallops. Really nice. Well presented and tasty. Perfect with my mocktail. Small portion but this was fine for me. The menu is designed more for sharing. There are tapas options, pizza (which appears to be popular looking around), other mains plus desserts. Not a huge menu but a sufficient and nice selection. It was pricey but I was happy to pay. Good meal, excellent service and lovely ambience. You don't need to dress up so much.

Chill out at The Long!
Dec 2016 • Business
It was a harrowing start to this last leg of my Marketing trip into IndoChina and my first foray into HCMC in Vietnam! I was almost cheated by two con men at the airport posing as airport limousine drivers and working as a pair to dupe unsuspecting new arrivals like me! Luckily, I am a seasoned traveler and immediately sensed something amiss when the driver, having been 'tasked' by the younger con, to bring me to my hotel, asked me for USD$5 to pay the exit booth! Utter rubbish as my defense wall came up instinctively and I shouted at him to turn around or I will smash his face, as he tried to make a go for my wad of US notes! Frightened at the sudden change in my tone and manner, he apologized and dropped me back at the arrival area! Agitated, I pulled violently at my heavy luggage and got out in a haze, straining my back in the process. The rest of the day was uneventful as a Grab taxi sent me to LAN LAN Hotel 1, a fabulous service oriented lodging for a first time visitor and a welcome respite! Dinner was simple pork chop plus rice at a nearby coffee shop and a can of local beer. Ok I downed two and the brands were agreeable! As is my usual habit, I decided to walk around town and find a nice music spot with a live band to chill out. Boy did it turned out to be a long long walk post dinner indeed! Still it was worth the effort as I soaked in the sights and sounds of historical Saigon on a Saturday evening, even being accosted for sex by a lady which I politely declined. Finally, after nearly an hour's walk, I came across The Long at Times Square! The sound of a heavenly diva encaptivated as the first Bartender Jack introduced me to a local stout version of my fave Irish Guinness. It was agreeable and I relaxed to the soothing songs and music of my romantic era - the 80s and 90s! She does belt out wonderful vocals for a local lass and I was lulled into a stupor. Meeting Brother Manh is the next blessing of the night! He is tall and has a leadership stance. Yet this unassuming man is so humble and shared with me his love for English and his battle with IELTS in the days ahead. He also told me of his lovely wife who is an English Teacher in a local school! That he could speak English so fluently tells me this young dude will soon go places. He has since scored 5.0 and is poised for greater growth. What an enchanting night and I promised to be back the next evening, a promise which I managed to keep in the late closing hour of this blessed joint! Certainly a yuppie PMEB oasis for a weary traveler where one is bound to meet nice people in this charming city whose people and places tell of change and continuity, of heroic resilience in the face of adversity and yet boosts of warm hospitality second to none! Manh is now a firm friend, a champion captain of life you must meet in Splendid Saigon! Rock on!

I've been to The Long many times and keep coming back, mostly due to the great location and the quality of service which can be lacking in many other places in HCMC. Arrogant attitude and discriminatory practice from one staff member during Happy Hour time!
Dec 2015 • Couples
Before I write the complaint I'd like to emphasize that the Long Bar used to be one of my favorites. I was a frequent customer. I stayed at the Reverie, I celebrated my BFF's birthday at Romeo&Julie, and I spent Happy Hour at the Long Bar countless times. Attached in this complaint are pictures of me at the Reverie/Long/R&J to prove that I'm not just any customer who has bias against the Long Bar. 

We were walking by the Long Bar with our dogs. There were a white manager (I guess he's the manager because he was dressed in suit) and a white chef. They are both friendly, courteous, and polite. We asked them if we and our dogs can sit at the Long Bar's seating outdoor area. The white chef (I guess he's the Italian chef at the R&J Restaurant) was so nice and said, "Of course, ..please welcome in!" 

As we were about to enter the outdoor seating area, a Vietnamese waitress gave a smirk and told us, "No Dog!". The white manager/chef exclaimed, "Why? I love dogs!!" The waitress didn't look at us and just told the chef, "It's the policy." So we just walked away. 

We respect the Long Bar's policy but we don't appreciate the attitude and the rudeness of that Vietnamese waitress. I was there before and that same waitress showed a discriminatory attitude towards Vietnamese people. One time there were 3 Vietnamese ladies who dressed casual and this waitress walked past by these customers with a smirky face like, "You guys don't belong here!" She is polite and courteous with other Western white-looking customers. We are US citizens but just because we can speak Vietnamese to her, she treats us different compared to other Western guests. 

Our dogs have sat at countless coffeeshops around the world from the 208 Restaurant in Rodeo Drive to the Continental in SaiGon. We've been to places that don't accept dogs but they tell us in the most polite manner possible. 

In this case, there was an disagreement in the staff. One told us that we can come in and one stopped us in the most uncivilized way. So you can understand how upset we were! And is it really stated in the policy? Or is it just because that rude waitress saw us thinking "they are just Vietnamese" and had that kind of attitude? 

Our complaint here is pretty unique and not applied to other customers. But other customers, if you look for a civilized outdoor lounge with timeless/classic look, I'd recommend the Continental. They welcome us and our dogs with the utmost courtesy: warm welcome, heartfelt greeting, a classic corner of SG, and a wonderful staff! 

For the Long Bar's manager, if you are care to reply this message, please do not state that it's just our policy for not accepting dogs in the outdoor seating. We are fully aware of that and respect your policy. What I complained here is the arrogant attitude of your waitress, the conflict in your staff's understanding of whatever policy about dogs, and the discriminatory practice of that one particular waitress.

If you are care enough to investigate this complaint, we will come back to the Long Bar and get this waitress' name. (unfortunately this time we were so shocked and just walked away, didn't care to get her name). But we are willing to come back and get her name so this kind of arrogant and rude treatment will not happen to anyone else.

Attached here are the pictures of me all over the Reverie to prove that I'm your valued customer and pictures of me and our dogs at Continental to show other customers that thanks God we found a more civilized and professional outdoor lounge in SG!

May Pham

Five star Italian food at reasonable price
Aug 2015 • Friends
I have visited The Long several times since its opening and I am now ready to provide my review.

If until recently I would have been hesitant whether to award 4 or 5 stars, after my last visit and the opportunity to try the new upgraded menu I have no doubt that the place deserves only the top rating.

The Long is located on one side of Times Square and it is accessible both from Dong Khoi and Nguyen Hue. It is both a lounge excellent for drinks and a bistro where to dine on authentic Italian food. The team in charge of the kitchen is the same staffing the other five star restaurants in Times Square and it is comprised of top notch real Italian chefs using authentic ingredients from Italy (I am Italian so I am in the position to make a judgement). So the deal is thar you can get great Italian food In a classy enviroment at reasonable prices. The place by the way is decorated with luxury finishings like the rest of the complex. I personally enjoy using the air conditioned room available upstairs, the rest of the space is reminescent of a veranda and it is an excellent place even for a few drinks with friends, just meter away from the two most vibrant streets in Saigon.. 

Let's come to the food. I would say that their forte is pizza baked in a stone oven. This is easily the best pizza in Saigon. Not too thin, not too thick and with tasty toppings. This is pizza like in Naples!

Especially with the upgraded menu they have some great pastas too. In my most recent visit I tried the squid ink Tagliolini with seafood (called cartoccio) that was spectacular and generous with seafood.

Also the appetizers are enticing. Pizza bread and a dip make an excellent starter if you are hungry (even if their portion are very generous, so no worries). 

In the dessert sector they prepare their own ice cream, I like to sample new flavors as the chef likes to play with new combinations. My recommandation is for pistacchio and gianduia. 

Staff is friendly and professional, so overall you get a five star experience and excellent authentic Italian food without breaking the bank. I look forward to coming back and also trying the other fine dining establishments available in Times Square.

reviews.review_text:

Gunnedah, Australia69 contributions

Good Product but Service Needs Attention
Feb 2015
This is a fairly new venue in town and I thought it time for a visit since they should have ironed out any kinks over the last few months. Three of us made a booking and went for dinner.

I'd heard good things about the pizzas and in my opinion they turned out to be correct. The pizzas were delicious and I could recommend the three we ordered to share (spinach and 6 cheeses; 5 seasons - yes, that's correct, not a typo; and burrata). 

The visit started well with the offer of a special: buy a bottle of Henkell or Moët Champagne or Yello Prosecco at a discounted price and get 4 bar snacks free. The prosecco was great value at 600,000 dong, the bar snacks were rubbish and I'm glad I didn't pay for them. They're on the menu but based on the samples I wouldn't order any in future. 

As we enjoyed our prosecco the ladies behind the bar were enjoying snacking on the cocktail garnishes including feeding them to each other; someone needs to tell them this is inappropriate hygiene at a place of this nature as is constantly playing with your hair when you're behind a bar handling food and drinks for patrons. 

We moved to a dining table to order our pizzas. We chose an Italian Merlot to have with the pizzas. The waiter returned saying they were out of stock. We asked him to clarify if they had the remaining four reds on the menu. He returned to say that there was another out of stock. It happened that the two out of stock were the 600,000 dong options so we selected an Australian Shiraz which, while very nice was, like the remaining wines in stock, well over twice the price. We explained to the waiter she needed to tell someone this wasn't good for a venue of this calibre. Inanely, she blamed Tet (Vietnamese New Year as if it has never happened before and caught them by surprise!!!). 

We noticed that the expat manager was summoned (not by us) and he sent two local staff to deal with the matter. We were trying to eat our pizza, the Shiraz still hadn't arrived so we asked that they concentrate on getting the Shiraz, not apologising. At the time the bill was settled we were charged for three glasses of the Shiraz rather than a bottle (it came to about 3/4 price of the bottle) which was a good gesture to recover but I think a place of this calibre - attached to a Leading Hotel simply shouldn't run out of a third of the red wines in their menu. 

Other mildly annoying service standards are when they insist on seating three people at a table for two (rather than a vacant table for four), bring all three pizzas (to share) at once and then inanely they're surprised when the table has no room for plates to eat the pizza!! 

Great venue. Great product. Great potential. But great need to get some stock control and staff training in place to get a better rating. I expected better from this venue.

Wonderful spot of a meal in HCMC - District 1
Nov 2014 • Couples
We walked by The Long @ Times Square and had to check it out. The bar, pizza station, ice cream and seating areas looked so inviting we headed there for breakfast the next morning.

I had the scrambled eggs with multigrain bread and my husband had the Big American breakfast, which included 3 eggs, vegetables, french toast and endless coffee. The food, especially the vegetables (roasted potatoes, onions and mushrooms) were very well prepared. The only negative was that my eggs and the french toast weren't quite warm. We still ate every bite. We had to ask for our coffee that came with the breakfast. We had earlier ordered cappuccino so I am assuming that they thought we wanted that in exchange for the coffee. The coffee was very strong, but delicious. It came with steamed milk. 

We had friends go there for dinner the evening before and they were also very happy with their meal.
